questionText: A spherical balloon is being inflated so that its volume is increasing at a constant rate of $12\pi$ cm³/s. Find the rate at which its radius is increasing at the moment when the radius is $3\text{ cm}$.
markingScheme:
State volume formula $V = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ **(1 mark)**
Differentiate with respect to $t$ using chain rule: $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \cdot \dfrac{dr}{dt}$ **(2 marks)**
Substitute $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 12\pi$ and $r = 3$ **(1 mark)**
Solve $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \tfrac{1}{3}\text{ cm/s}$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.step: Write down the relationship between the variables
solutionSteps.explanation: The volume of a sphere is $V = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. Both $V$ and $r$ are changing with time $t$.
